author: C. S. Girard
title: Scott Fitzgerald criticizes Korean government actions and supports new litigation funding bill
text:
Scott Lawrence Fitzgerald, U.S. Representative of Wisconsin's 5th congressional district | Official U.S. House headshot
Scott Lawrence Fitzgerald, U.S. Representative of Wisconsin's 5th congressional district | Official U.S. House headshot
Rep. Scott Fitzgerald, a U.S. Congressman from Wisconsin, has recently shared several updates on his official Twitter account, ranging from criticism of international legal actions to legislative advocacy and industry engagement.
On January 12, 2026, Fitzgerald expressed strong disapproval of the Korean government's decision to pursue criminal charges against American executives at Coupang. He stated, "I am appalled at the recent actions by the Korean government to call for criminal charges against American executives of @Coupang based on a politically motivated witch hunt. The United States government will continue to pursue measures to hold the Korean government accountable".
Two days later, on January 14, 2026, Fitzgerald highlighted his participation in an event hosted by the American Council of Life Insurers (ACLI). He wrote, "I was honored to speak to members of the American Council of Life Insurers today about retirement security and the vital role the industry plays in driving Wisconsin jobs. Thanks for hosting @ACLINews."
Later that same day, Fitzgerald voiced support for legislation introduced by Rep. Darrell Issa aimed at regulating third-party litigation funding. In his tweet he said, "I’m proud to support my colleague @repdarrellissa's bill, the Protecting Third Party Litigation Funding from Abuse Act, and urge its passage.
Undisclosed litigation funding can shift control from plaintiffs to silent investors, including foreign actors. This bill requires".
Scott Fitzgerald has represented Wisconsin in Congress since winning election victories in both 2020 and 2022; he defeated Tom Palzewicz in 2020 with over 60% of the vote and Mike Van Someren in 2022 with more than 64%.
